text:
acme_infra: Hey team — since yesterday afternoon our app started getting a lot of 5xx/slow responses from the Redwood API. Looks like requests are being queued and timing out under load. We increased concurrency from 20 -> 80 and saw this. Anyone seen perceived throttling when using continuous batching + KV cache?

Maya: Hi! Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste an example request/response headers and the org id? In particular any x-rate-limit-*, x-queue-time, x-cache-* headers. Also are you using Dedicated or Hosted?

acme_infra: Hosted. Sample response headers below (redacted):

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-rate-limit-limit: 100
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-queue-time: 320ms
x-cache-hit: false
x-request-id: rwd-8a3b
```

Body was: {"error":"Request queued: backpressure"} — not a straight 429. We also see big tail latency spikes (1.2s -> 3s) intermittently. Billing/quotas show we haven't hit org quota.

Lucas: Thanks — this matches a few recent incidents. Quick tl;dr: continuous batching aggregates requests until either batch full or max latency reached. Under bursts, the runtime temporarily queues incoming requests to build batches which can look like throttling if your client expects instant responses. KV cache warm/cold behavior also affects it: if a request misses KV (cold) the runtime may do extra work which increases per-request service time and reduces effective throughput.

Sam: Also note that the Hosted rate limiter uses a token-bucket per-org and a soft burst window. When the bucket drains (x-rate-limit-remaining=0) requests aren't hard-blocked immediately — the system may queue them for a short period to preserve latency SLOs. That queue is what you're seeing as 503/backpressure.

Maya: Can you try two quick repros so we can narrow it down: 
1) Single-client, serial requests (concurrency=1) hitting the same session key — measure p50/p95.
2) Ramp concurrency to 80 over 30s with the same payload and session key. Post both results here. Also include whether you set any request headers like `X-Session-ID` or `Prefer-Low-Latency` if used.

acme_infra: Here's the curl we used to repro (concurrency via parallel run):

```
for i in {1..80}; do
  echo "payload $i" | xargs -I{} -P80 curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Session-ID: user-123" -d '{"input":"{}"}' &
done
```

With concurrency=20 -> p95 ~ 350ms. With 80 -> p95 ~ 1.9s and ~40% responses with 503/backpressure.

Lucas: Repro looks good. Two quick suggestions you can try now: 
- Set your client to send a unique session per logical user instead of reusing a single session for all concurrent requests. KV cache benefits when session affinity is preserved, but reusing one session across many parallel requests can cause lock contention inside the runtime.
- If you need low tail latency under bursty concurrency, set `Prefer-Low-Latency: true` which disables waiting to form larger batches (this increases cost).

Sam: We're also going to check internal metrics for your org window around the timestamps. @deploy-bot can you pull the runtime queue-length and batch-size histograms for org acme (1769502000 -> 1769507400)?

deploy-bot: Metrics query submitted: `GET /internal/metrics?org=acme&start=1769502000&end=1769507400&series=queue_length,batch_size` — returning ETA ~20s.

Lucas: Extra detail — the KV cache is sharded per-model-per-session-key. If you hammer the same session key from many machines the cache misses and internal ops to populate KV can serialise a bit, which looks like throttling. Warmup pattern: send a short prefix request (same session header) to prime KV, then ramp concurrent generation.

Maya: Another workaround while we dig in: add jittered ramping (e.g., add randomized ~10-100ms sleeps between starts) and fallback to lower concurrency when you see 5xx. Can you try a quick warmup (5 warm requests) then ramp to 80 and report?

acme_infra: Did warmup with 5 prefix requests, then ramp. p95 improved to ~650ms and 503 count dropped to ~6%. Better but still spikes. Any config on our org side that could increase burst tokens? We're on the standard plan.

Sam: Standard plan has modest burst capacity. We can temporarily increase your burst allowance for testing — will need an approval. If you want we can also enable a short-lived higher-priority token for a stress window. Would you like us to do that for the next 30m while you test?

acme_infra: Yes please. That would help validate whether it's purely quota/burst related.

Maya: Filed a support escalation and requested temporary burst uplift for org acme (case #SUP-1429). Lucas & Sam will coordinate the runtime checks.

Lucas: For long term: if your pattern is many small, low-latency requests, prefer lower batching (max_batch_latency_ms=5-10ms) and more sessions. If cost matters, keep batching higher (20-50ms) but expect higher tail under sudden bursts. Also consider client-side token-bucket to smooth bursts before hitting our API.

Sam: Follow-up repro steps for you to run and paste back: 
1) Warm KV: send 10 short prefix requests with X-Session-ID.
2) Measure serial p95.
3) Run the ramp script that increases concurrency from 5 -> 80 over 60s (example below).

```
# ramp.sh example
for c in 5 10 20 40 60 80; do
  seq 1 $c | xargs -P$c -n1 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Session-ID: user-123" -d '{"input":"ramp test"}' &
  sleep 10
done
```

4) Capture response headers and any 5xx counts.

acme_infra: Running the ramp now with uplift enabled... will post results in ~40m. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Maya: Thanks — we'll keep monitoring. If the uplift removes the 503/backpressure entirely it was likely burst/quota interplay; if you still see queuing we will dig into batching/kvs locks on the runtime side.

acme_infra: Quick update after 40m: uplift helped a lot. 503s are down to ~1% and avg p95 ~450ms. Still seeing occasional 1.2s tail spikes at the highest concurrency.

Lucas: Ok that's useful. We'll follow up with a patch to tweak how KV population work is parallelised; for now, two options: 
- Keep warmup + session-affinity 
- Use Prefer-Low-Latency for critical paths

Sam: Logged a ticket to investigate KV population locking and potential optimistic parallel fills. Ticket: RUNTIME-6421.

acme_infra: Great—appreciate the fast help. Can you update us in this thread when RUNTIME-6421 has an ETA?

Maya: Will do. Marking the escalation as active and I'll follow up with a post-mortem once the engine changes land. :spiral_notepad:
